title: Minimum wage increase on restaurant employment

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy
- Method: Difference-in-Differences (DID) with two-way fixed effects (unit and period), exploiting the common treatment timing (state minimum wage increase in period 4) for treated states versus neighboring control states.
- Why: We observe a balanced panel of restaurants before and after the policy, with clear treated vs. control units and multiple pre/post periods; DID is the standard approach for estimating the causal effect under these conditions.
- Key assumptions:
  - Parallel trends: In the absence of the minimum wage increase, treated and control restaurants would have had the same trend in employment.
  - No spillovers: The policy in treated states does not affect employment in control states.
  - Stable composition and no differential shocks coinciding with treatment that differentially affect treated units.
  - SUTVA and common treatment timing (all treated adopt in period 4).

We will:
- Estimate a baseline TWFE DID: y_it = β · (treated_i × post_t) + α_i + γ_t + ε_it on log FTE employment.
- Conduct a dynamic/event-study robustness to check pre-trends (using period-by-treated interactions with period 3 as the omitted pre-period).
- Provide a narrow window DID (periods 3–4) and a simple 2×2 DID on pre/post averages as robustness.

## 2. R Code
```r
# Complete, self-contained R code

# 0) Packages
pkgs <- c("fixest", "dplyr", "MASS")
for(p in pkgs){
  if(!requireNamespace(p, quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages(p, repos = "https://cloud.r-project.org")
  }
  library(p, character.only = TRUE)
}

options(scipen = 99, digits = 4)

# 1) Read data
df <- read.csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s02_data.csv")

# Ensure types are reasonable
# (fixest can take integer FE directly; no need to coerce to factor)
stopifnot(all(c("unit_id","period","treated","post","treat_x_post","y") %in% names(df)))

# Helper: percent interpretation for log-point coefficient
to_pct <- function(b){ 100 * (exp(b) - 1) }

# 2) Baseline DID: TWFE (unit and period FE), cluster by unit
fit_did <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
  data = df,
  cluster = ~ unit_id
)

b_did <- coef(fit_did)[["treat_x_post"]]
se_did <- sqrt(vcov(fit_did)["treat_x_post","treat_x_post"])
ci_did <- b_did + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se_did

cat("==== Baseline DID (TWFE) ====\n")
cat(sprintf("DID estimate (log points): %.4f\n", b_did))
cat(sprintf("Standard error (clustered by unit): %.4f\n", se_did))
cat(sprintf("95%% CI (log points): [%.4f, %.4f]\n", ci_did[1], ci_did[2]))
cat(sprintf("Percent change: %.2f%% (95%% CI: %.2f%%, %.2f%%)\n\n", to_pct(b_did), to_pct(ci_did[1]), to_pct(ci_did[2])))

# 3) Event-study style robustness:
# Create treated-by-period dummies with period 3 (last pre) as reference.
# We include only treated*1[period==k] for k != 3, and keep unit+period FE.
es_periods <- setdiff(1:8, 3)  # omit 3 as the base period
for (k in es_periods) {
  vname <- paste0("ev_p", k)
  df[[vname]] <- as.integer(df$treated == 1 & df$period == k)
}

# Fit event-study with interactions
es_vars <- paste0("ev_p", es_periods)
f_es <- as.formula(paste("y ~", paste(es_vars, collapse = " + "), "| unit_id + period"))
fit_es <- feols(f_es, data = df, cluster = ~ unit_id)

b_es <- coef(fit_es)
V_es <- vcov(fit_es)

# Pre-trend joint test for periods 1 and 2 relative to period 3
pre_vars <- c("ev_p1","ev_p2")
has_pre <- all(pre_vars %in% names(b_es))
if (has_pre) {
  b_pre <- b_es[pre_vars]
  V_pre <- V_es[pre_vars, pre_vars, drop = FALSE]
  # Wald statistic with generalized inverse for safety
  W_stat <- as.numeric(t(b_pre) %*% ginv(V_pre) %*% b_pre)
  p_pre <- 1 - pchisq(W_stat, df = length(pre_vars))
} else {
  W_stat <- NA; p_pre <- NA
}

# On-impact (period 4) and average post (periods 4–8)
post_vars <- paste0("ev_p", 4:8)
post_vars <- post_vars[post_vars %in% names(b_es)]
w <- rep(1/length(post_vars), length(post_vars))
b_post_avg <- as.numeric(sum(w * b_es[post_vars]))
V_post <- V_es[post_vars, post_vars, drop = FALSE]
se_post_avg <- sqrt(as.numeric(t(w) %*% V_post %*% w))
ci_post_avg <- b_post_avg + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se_post_avg

b_on_impact <- if ("ev_p4" %in% names(b_es)) b_es[["ev_p4"]] else NA
se_on_impact <- if (!is.na(b_on_impact)) sqrt(V_es["ev_p4","ev_p4"]) else NA
ci_on_impact <- if (!is.na(b_on_impact)) b_on_impact + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se_on_impact else c(NA, NA)

cat("==== Event-Study Robustness ====\n")
cat("Reference period: 3 (last pre)\n")
if(!is.na(b_on_impact)){
  cat(sprintf("On-impact (period 4) effect (log pts): %.4f; SE: %.4f; 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
              b_on_impact, se_on_impact, ci_on_impact[1], ci_on_impact[2]))
  cat(sprintf("On-impact percent change: %.2f%% (95%% CI: %.2f%%, %.2f%%)\n",
              to_pct(b_on_impact), to_pct(ci_on_impact[1]), to_pct(ci_on_impact[2])))
}
cat(sprintf("Average post effect (periods 4–8, equal-weight) (log pts): %.4f; SE: %.4f; 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            b_post_avg, se_post_avg, ci_post_avg[1], ci_post_avg[2]))
cat(sprintf("Average post percent change: %.2f%% (95%% CI: %.2f%%, %.2f%%)\n",
            to_pct(b_post_avg), to_pct(ci_post_avg[1]), to_pct(ci_post_avg[2])))
if(!is.na(p_pre)){
  cat(sprintf("Pre-trend joint Wald test (periods 1 & 2 = 0): p-value = %.4f\n\n", p_pre))
} else {
  cat("Pre-trend test not available (coefficients missing).\n\n")
}

# 4) Narrow-window DID (periods 3 vs 4 only): focuses on immediate change
df$near_window <- df$period %in% c(3,4)
fit_near <- feols(
  y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
  data = subset(df, near_window),
  cluster = ~ unit_id
)
b_near <- coef(fit_near)[["treat_x_post"]]
se_near <- sqrt(vcov(fit_near)["treat_x_post","treat_x_post"])
ci_near <- b_near + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se_near

cat("==== Narrow-Window DID (Periods 3–4) ====\n")
cat(sprintf("Immediate DID estimate (log pts): %.4f; SE: %.4f; 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            b_near, se_near, ci_near[1], ci_near[2]))
cat(sprintf("Immediate percent change: %.2f%% (95%% CI: %.2f%%, %.2f%%)\n\n",
            to_pct(b_near), to_pct(ci_near[1]), to_pct(ci_near[2])))

# 5) Simple 2x2 DID on pre/post averages (no FE), cross-sectional regression on unit-level diffs
df_prepost <- df %>%
  group_by(unit_id, treated) %>%
  summarize(y_pre = mean(y[post == 0], na.rm = TRUE),
            y_post = mean(y[post == 1], na.rm = TRUE),
            diff = y_post - y_pre,
            .groups = "drop")

fit_collapsed <- lm(diff ~ treated, data = df_prepost)
b_collapse <- coef(fit_collapsed)[["treated"]]
se_collapse <- sqrt(vcov(fit_collapsed)["treated","treated"])
ci_collapse <- b_collapse + c(-1.96, 1.96) * se_collapse

cat("==== Collapsed 2x2 DID (Unit pre/post averages) ====\n")
cat(sprintf("Collapsed DID estimate (log pts): %.4f; SE: %.4f; 95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n",
            b_collapse, se_collapse, ci_collapse[1], ci_collapse[2]))
cat(sprintf("Percent change: %.2f%% (95%% CI: %.2f%%, %.2f%%)\n",
            to_pct(b_collapse), to_pct(ci_collapse[1]), to_pct(ci_collapse[2])))
```

## 3. Expected Findings
- Sign: Small to zero effect on fast-food employment. Theory suggests downward pressure on employment, but much empirical work (e.g., Card & Krueger; Dube et al.) finds near-zero short-run effects in this sector.
- Magnitude: Approximately 0 to -2% in log FTE employment (i.e., β between about 0.00 and -0.02), with confidence intervals likely spanning zero. Event-study pre-trends should be statistically indistinguishable from zero. The narrow-window estimate should be similar in sign and magnitude.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: DID — treated=high-wage states, control=neighboring states; shock=minimum wage hike
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Modest employment decline in treated restaurants post minimum wage increase
